statutes.act: And Section 302 Read With Section 149 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The appellants, five in number, have challenged their conviction recorded by the High Court under Section 148 and Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code for the murder of Mahadu.

For the offence under Section 148 they have been directed to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and for the offence under Sections 302/149 they have been directed to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life.
They have also been convicted under Sections 323/34, IPC, for causing injuries to Runjaba and each of them has been directed to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year.
Original accused 1 having since died, no order of conviction was recorded against him.

The prosecution version regarding the incident is unfolded throughout the evidence of six eye-witnesses, viz., PW 3 Runjaba, the injured brother of the deceased, PW 6 Kasturabai, widow of the deceased, PW 5 Sahaji Saluba, a distant relative, PW 8 Bagaji Rama, cousin of the deceased, PW 7 Sonaba Thakaji and PW 2 Sampat Ananda.
From their evidence it appears that on the morning of March 10, 1973 the deceased had gone out to ease himself while his wife, Kasturabai was preparing tea.
At that time the family members of the assessed as well as his brother Runjaba who were at their respective houses, heard a commotion and rushed to the scene of occurrence.
Many neighbours living in that lane, known as Dhanger lane, also had come out.
issues: Whether the evidence of the six eye-witnesses is reliable
Whether the accused persons were involved in the assault on the deceased and his brother Runjaba
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that the evidence of the six eye-witnesses was unreliable and that the trial court had discarded the evidence on minor contradictions
They also argued that there was no motive for the accused persons to commit the crime
respondent_arguments: The prosecution argued that the evidence of the six eye-witnesses was reliable and that the accused persons were involved in the assault on the deceased and his brother Runjaba
They also argued that there was a motive for the accused persons to commit the crime
court_reasoning: The court held that the evidence of the six eye-witnesses was reliable and that the accused persons were involved in the assault on the deceased and his brother Runjaba
It also held that there was no prior concert; it happened all of a sudden and the deceased and his brother received injuries in the incident
The court concluded that the intention of the assailants was to give thrashing and it is not possible to cull out an intention to kill
holding: The conviction under Section 302 IPC was set aside and substituted with a conviction under Section 325 read with Section 34 IPC
The sentence recorded by the High Court under Sections 302/149 was also set aside and substituted with a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for five years
